# Results — Study 477 (Choppiness Index)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The believers' claim — **a low
Choppiness Index marks a "trending" regime that precedes tradable momentum** — encoded as a
mechanical rule. CI = 100·log₁₀(Σ TR / (max high − min low)) / log₁₀(N) over a trailing N = 14
window (trailing only, no look-ahead); a long fires on the **onset** of a low-CI reading
(CI < 38.2, the canonical trending threshold), entered at the **next close** (one documented
lag), and we measure the forward 5/10/20/60-day return. Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted (**total-return**) closes for **SPY, QQQ, IWM, DIA, GLD** (public, no key) |
| Window | 2005-01-03 → 2026-05-29 (**As-of 2026-05-31**, partial June dropped; **21.4** years) |
| SPY fingerprint | `4cb5244f3990` (sha1[:12] of the close column, As-of slice) |
| Entries | **936** mechanical low-CI onsets pooled across the 5 tapes (N = 14, CI < 38.2) |
| Timing / costs | CI uses only the trailing 14-bar window; enter the **next close** (one lag); hold 5/10/20/60 days; **1 bp** one-way × 2 legs per entry |

> **Price-only vs total-return.** The ETFs are auto-adjusted (dividends reinvested) — labelled
> total-return everywhere. The Signal axis uses a basket of **surviving** liquid ETFs; this is a
> single-instrument regime study, not a cross-sectional anomaly, so survivorship affects only the
> drift baseline (which is exactly what the random-entry control neutralizes).

## The signal — low-CI onset vs a drift-matched random baseline (the honest test)

One-sample *t* is the **misleading** number (it measures the index's upward drift); the
**Welch low-CI-vs-random** *t* is the test that matters. Δ = low-CI − random.

| horizon | n | low-CI | win% | one-sample *t* | random | Δ (low-CI−random) | net of cost | Welch *t* | *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day  | 936 | +45.4 bps | 60% | +5.25 | +27.7 bps | **+17.7 bps** | +43.4 bps | +1.54 | 0.124 |
| 10-day | 936 | +61.5 bps | 63% | +5.07 | +61.2 bps | **+0.3 bps** | +59.5 bps | +0.02 | 0.983 |
| 20-day | 935 | +106.7 bps | 63% | +5.56 | +114.4 bps | **−7.7 bps** | +104.7 bps | −0.33 | 0.741 |
| 60-day | 928 | +293.8 bps | 68% | +7.93 | +250.1 bps | **+43.8 bps** | +291.8 bps | +1.15 | 0.250 |

Read it carefully. The one-sample *t* against zero looks spectacular (**+5.56** at 20 days,
**+7.93** at 60) — but that is **pure beta**: long-only entries on an upward-drifting index
inherit the drift. Against the **drift-matched random baseline**, the low-CI onset is
indistinguishable from buying on random days: Δ = +17.7 / +0.3 / −7.7 / +43.8 bps at
5/10/20/60 days, and the difference **never clears the desk's *t* ≥ 2 bar** (max Welch *t* =
+1.54 at 5 days, *p* = 0.124). The Choppiness Index does not time trend vs chop usefully.

## Per-ticker (H = 20) — no coherent cross-sectional edge

| ticker | entries | low-CI | one-sample *t* | random | Δ (low-CI−random) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY | 182 | +84.3 bps | +2.36 | +105.0 bps | **−20.7 bps** |
| QQQ | 186 | +101.8 bps | +1.88 | +144.8 bps | **−43.0 bps** |
| IWM | 153 | +99.8 bps | +1.82 | +99.5 bps | **+0.3 bps** |
| DIA | 184 | +128.4 bps | +5.01 | +96.4 bps | **+32.0 bps** |
| GLD | 231 | +115.5 bps | +2.78 | +121.7 bps | **−6.1 bps** |

Only **DIA** edges out a meaningfully positive delta (+32.0 bps); in 3 of 5 names the low-CI
onset *underperforms* a random entry. The split is the hallmark of relabelled drift — no
coherent cross-sectional signal.

## Geometry placebo — scramble the trend-vs-chop structure, nothing changes

The decisive "does the CI's structure matter?" test: recompute CI and its low-CI onsets on a
**return-shuffled surrogate** price — permute the daily returns, destroying the trend-vs-chop
geometry the index reads while keeping the price marginal — then bank the *real* forward return
at those surrogate-detected dates. If the CI's structure were load-bearing, the scramble would
collapse the result.

| test | observed low-CI 20d return | placebo *p* | draws |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY return-shuffled surrogate | +84.3 bps | **0.409** | 500 |

**41% of structure-scrambled surrogates match or beat the real one** (*p* = 0.409). The specific
trend-vs-chop reading carries no forecasting information — a return-permuted nonsense CI does
just as well. "CI times trend vs chop" is busted.

## Synthetic positive control — the harness CAN bank a planted "low-CI precedes momentum"

On a deterministic tape that plants the *exact* believers' structure (whenever the trailing
window is clean/straight, an upward momentum burst follows — knob `edge`), the same low-CI rule
behaves exactly as it must — so the flat real-tape result is a genuine "nothing there", not a
dead detector.

| planted edge | n | low-CI | win% | one-sample *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.00** (no planted momentum) | 80 | +63.5 bps | 57% | +1.12 |
| **0.35** (real planted "low-CI → momentum") | 84 | +871.0 bps | 79% | **+7.47** |

With no planted momentum the control sits at *t* ≈ 1 (no false positive); the planted
"low-CI precedes momentum" lights up at *t* = +7.47 with a 79% win-rate. The detector is live.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The low-CI onset does **not** beat a drift-matched random baseline
  (low-CI − random = +17.7 / +0.3 / −7.7 / +43.8 bps at 5/10/20/60 days; the Welch *t* never
  clears 2, max +1.54 at 5 days, *p* = 0.124). The impressive one-sample *t*'s (20-day +5.56,
  60-day +7.93) are pure beta — the upward drift of long equity indices.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** There is no residual edge once the drift you were always getting is
  removed, and costs only deepen the hole. The same drift is captured more cheaply and more
  fully by holding the index; the CI filter trades less and pays costs on each entry, dominating
  nothing. No capacity question because there is no edge to scale.
- **"Does CI forecast trend vs chop usefully?" — BUSTED.** The return-shuffled placebo leaves
  the result intact (*p* = 0.409): structure-scrambled surrogates do as well as the real CI, so
  the trend-vs-chop reading carries no forecasting information. The Choppiness Index is a
  descriptive volatility-geometry gauge, not a regime-timing strategy.
